dimensions.assessment: Affects registered entities, commodity exchanges, and individuals or entities trading or listing event contracts based on elections, government activities, gaming, and other restricted topics.
dimensions.evidence: prohibit event contracts based on terrorism, assassination, war, gaming, illegal activity, election outcomes, government activities

dimensions.assessment: Prohibits certain categories of event contracts from being listed or traded on registered entities, altering market offerings.
dimensions.evidence: it shall be unlawful to list or make available for trading on or through a registered entity an agreement

dimensions.assessment: No specific federal spending or revenue changes are stated in the source text.
Amends the Commodity Exchange Act to restrict certain derivative and event contracts and grants rulemaking authority to the Commodity Futures Trading Commission.
dimensions.evidence: To amend the Commodity Exchange Act to prohibit event contracts based on terrorism

dimensions.assessment: Provides a permanent statutory prohibition taking effect 180 days after enactment.
dimensions.evidence: The amendments made by subsection (a) shall take effect on the date that is 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act.

missing_information: Economic impact on trading volume or market revenue.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill amends the Commodity Exchange Act to prohibit specific types of event contracts on registered entities, while allowing states to exempt themselves from gaming contract bans.
